instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Hidden Power
cards.instruction: Act publicly modest while making choices as though you control the outcome.

cards.title: Confess First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to confess or incriminate themselves before you reveal anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only taking notes, now the kitchen's safe. I'll put the printer incident first. What happened to it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Paper jam. Why was there smoke in the kitchen?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll leave that page blank for a moment. Did you put something in the printer that shouldn't have gone in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I used sticky labels. Can we talk about the smoke now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Were they marked 'not for printers'? Give me that sentence for your page, then I'll turn over to mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only making Mum's apology dinner. I'll serve once we've sorted out what we're saying about her birthday. Why was there no restaurant booking?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I forgot. What happened to her present?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The potatoes can wait. Did you forget to book, or did you assume I'd do it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I assumed you'd do it. Now your turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even after telling Mum it was confirmed? Say that bit aloud and I'll bring the plates in. Then you can hear what happened to the present.

cards.title: Sell the Disaster
cards.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only helping with the restaurant budget. I've booked the roof removal; it's the affordable answer to our ventilation problem.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happens when it rains?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep us closed. No customer should have to eat in the wet; we do have responsibilities.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Rain is forecast all opening week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll use the wages we save to buy umbrellas for the tables. Cancel now and we lose those savings. I'll tell the roofers we're going ahead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only helping with the auction tickets. I've sent the charity our expected takings, so we can tell everyone the money's already doing good.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You borrowed five thousand. Only your mum has registered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll cancel most of the catering. One bidder needs very few sandwiches; that's responsible use of the budget.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum's only coming to give us a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll bid ourselves. I'll raise the card limit before we open. We have to repay that loan without asking the charity to return our donation.

cards.title: Fake the Expertise
cards.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only here to hold the tools. I'll get your boiler running; leave these controls to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've been adjusting the kitchen timer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Establishing the heating interval. Call the engineer; I'll have him handle the boiler while I coordinate the checks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's on the phone. He wants to know what temperature you measured.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him we're establishing the baseline. Put him on speaker; I'll ask the questions. You take the readings he needs, and I'll decide when we've checked enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only carrying your violin, but I'll tune it before the audition. Don't take it in until I've finished.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've tightened that string until it snapped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It couldn't hold pitch. I've spared you a failure onstage; I'll decide which replacement will stand up to the piece.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The panel heard it snap. They're asking if you know what you're doing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them I rejected an unreliable string. Ask for their spare violin; I'll check that one before I let you take it in.

cards.title: Everything Is a Contest
cards.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only peeling the potatoes. First to peel five chooses dinner, though, and I've done four. You still want pizza?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Unless you can find a cheaper dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: These cost nothing tonight; they're already here. I'll put that down as a win for potatoes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got a voucher. Pizza's free.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then best free dinner wins. I'll cook these, you order yours, and I'll get Mum to judge. She always asks for my potatoes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only the tea-pourer. Mine's the stronger cup; I can manage it without milk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the same pot. I added milk so I could drink mine sooner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll time us: first to finish wins. I've only got two mouthfuls left.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've finished. I'm making another.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll score refills instead. Fewest wins, and I can make these two mouthfuls last all breakfast. Shall I put you down for one already?

cards.title: Brighter Side
cards.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only holding the map. The car won't start, so I've chosen us a walking route. Lovely chance to stretch our legs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's raining.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better, a free shower. I'll take us through the park; no stuffy bus for us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My shoe's leaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful, a footbath as well. I'll take us past the bandstand so you can sit down and enjoy it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only carrying the scenery. We've sold no tickets, so I'll use tonight for an uninterrupted rehearsal. What a gift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre's cancelled us. I'm asking for our deposit back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better. I'll book the room above the pub; people already go there voluntarily.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've kept the deposit. All we can afford is the bus home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful, a touring production. I'll choose the scene short enough for two stops. You bring exact change; I'll get the scenery on first.
